we propose a new deep multi task representation learning framework based on generalising matrix factorisation to tensor factorisation.

the following three questions.
the problem of multi-task learning in the era of the deep learning.
developing a deep multi-task learning framework that can automatically learn knowledge sharing structure in a deep network, and thus, is applicable in many domains.

the paper presents an approach to multi-task learning that is based on a tensor factorisation approach and that this approach is shown to outperform other approaches in terms of accuracy and the number of design choices required.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we propose a novel deep multi-task learning approach that is able to learn end-to-end knowledge-sharing structures at every layer in deep neural networks, and is applicable to both homogeneous and heterogenous multi-task learning problems.

we are the first to propose a deep learning based MTL framework that can learn cross-task sharing structure automatically and end-to-end, and can be applied to both homogeneous and heterogenous MTL settings.
we have developed a deep learning approach that learns cross-task knowledge sharing automatically, and that can be applied to both homogeneous and heterogenous multi-task learning problems.
The main takeaway from our work is that
tensor factorisation can be used to learn end-to-end knowledge transfer in deep networks.
the matrix factorisation approach to MTL can be generalised to deep learning, to realise a more powerful deep MTL approach.
deep learning and MTL can be seamlessly combined, and this combination can be very effective in practice.
